subject: Syndicate Runner + Redwood: runtime adapter & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration
messages:
From: Chris Patel <chris@syndicate.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-14T09:17:00Z
Subject: Intro: Syndicate Runner + Redwood integration idea

Hi Sofia,

Hope you're well — I'm Chris, Head of Integrations at Syndicate AI. We build Runner, a developer SDK that packages orchestration, telemetry, and connector utilities for LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations. A number of our ISV customers have asked for a first-class runtime adapter to Redwood so they can push to Redwood Dedicated/Private without reworking instrumented code.

High level: we propose building a small runtime adapter in Runner that plugs directly into Redwood's model routing and tracing hooks (span correlation + token attribution). That gives customers:
- One-click binding from Runner to Redwood endpoints
- Out-of-the-box LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors preconfigured for batching and KV cache preservation
- Tracing/attribution forwarded to Redwood Console for cost/latency matching

I've attached a short spec and a draft pilot SoW for your review. Would love 30 minutes next week to walk through scope and timelines.

Attachments: syndicate-integration-spec-v1.pdf, syndicate-pilot-sow-draft.docx

Thanks,
Chris Patel
Head of Integrations | Syndicate AI
chris@syndicate.ai
https://syndicate.ai
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-14T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: Syndicate Runner + Redwood integration idea

Chris — thanks for the clear summary and the spec. Curious idea and looks like good developer UX overlap.

Looping in Marissa (ISV Partnerships) and Karthik (runtime/telemetry) so we can assess technical fit and commercial model. Quick asks before we book time:
1) Does the Runner adapter require any privileged access to the Redwood control plane, or is it purely client-side config + headers for tracing?
2) Any existing customers already using your Runner with other hosted runtimes (we can ask for references)?
3) Target pilot scale — e.g., sample throughput / expected token volumes for the initial test.

Marissa/Karthik — would you be able to join a 30-min sync next Tue or Wed? I can schedule.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, Chris Patel <chris@syndicate.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-15T15:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: Syndicate Runner + Redwood integration idea

Thanks for including me. I scanned the spec — high level reaction: good potential for quick wins on GTM (co-markets + sample deploys), and the SoW looks straightforward. A couple technical concerns Karthik and I flagged:
- Token attribution: we need a deterministic span->token mapping so our cost dashboards reflect adapter-originated tokens (not just the final model call). Is Runner emitting per-request metadata?
- KV cache preservation: we should ensure the adapter can send initial KV state or a cache key to avoid recomputing embeddings on cold starts.
- Auth patterns: we prefer adapter to use short-lived tokens + optional service-to-service mTLS for Dedicated/Private customers.

Please send over any customer reference who has integrated a Runner adapter with another vendor; helps expedite engineering sign-off.

Availability: Tue 2027-04-20 14:00-15:00 PT works for me.

—Marissa
Senior ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Chris Patel <chris@syndicate.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@promptlab.co>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-16T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: Syndicate Runner + Redwood integration idea

Hi all,

Great questions — answers inline:
1) Access model: Runner adapter is client-side by default. For Dedicated/Private we offer an optional connector that performs token exchange and uses a short-lived cert to call the control plane (no persistent credentials stored). We can scope either option in the pilot.
2) References: PromptLab (Alicia, cc'd) is piloting Runner with two other managed runtimes; Alicia can speak to deployment and observability.
3) Pilot scale: we propose a 2-week pilot at ~10-20 qps with a mix of short and long context prompts (avg seq length ~800 tokens) to validate batching and latency SLOs.

Attached is a small update to the spec addressing token attribution headers (X-Runner-Span / X-Token-Attribution). Also adding a sample sandbox invite link: https://app.syndicate.ai/sandbox/redwood-sandbox-invite

Would love the Tue 4/20 slot — I'll take it.

Best,
Chris
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Chris Patel <chris@syndicate.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T16:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: Syndicate Runner + Redwood integration idea

All — good sync today, appreciate the demo and the sandbox access. Key notes and action items (mutual action plan below). Forwarding the thread to capture agreed technical scope.

Quick recaps / decisions we made on the call:
- Pilot scope: build Runner adapter that supports both a client-only flow and an optional control-plane token-exchange path for Dedicated/Private. Pilot will run for 2 weeks against our dev Dedicated cluster.
- Tracing: we agreed on header conventions (X-Runner-Span, X-Runner-Parent, X-Token-Attribution) and Karthik's team will add a small shim in Redwood Console to accept and surface these spans under an "Partner Integrations" grouping.
- KV caching: Runner will include a cache-key header and an initial KV payload for warm starts. We'll validate cache preservation across restarts in the pilot.
- Security: Runner team to provide an architecture note on token exchange and optional mTLS; Redwood sec will do a 3-day review.

Action items:
1) Syndicate: share updated spec + pilot SoW in Drive (Chris) — due 2027-04-22.
2) Redwood (Karthik): provide dev Dedicated cluster credentials and a small test harness (curl + sample traces) — due 2027-04-23.
3) Marissa: draft a co-marketing brief and commercial terms for the pilot (credits, roadmap call) — due 2027-04-26.

Attachments referenced during call: syndicate-integration-spec-v1.pdf, syndicate-pilot-sow-draft.docx.

If there are any discrepancies in my notes please reply-all with corrections. Looking forward to the pilot.

—Karthik Iyer
